resources.string: Design your own face for the Boox sleep screen. BooxUltimatum draws it to fit the screen and keeps it up to date while you use the tablet.
A face that fills the screen. Boox shows it as its sleep screen picture and reads it again each time the tablet goes to sleep.

A small paper plate laid over the screen as it was when the tablet went to sleep, using Boox’s Transparent style. Boox lays a sticker, a see-through picture, over that screen, and BooxUltimatum draws the plate on it. BooxUltimatum needs Shizuku, or your permission to change the sticker, to draw the plate.
The weekday, a big day number, the month with today marked, and what is coming up.
The battery on a radio tuning scale in the style of Braun, with the date and ruled readings below.
The weekday set as large as the screen allows, with the quote of the day or your own below it.

Leaves the top of the screen to the Boox clock, which Boox redraws every 5 minutes while the tablet sleeps (seen on a Note Air6 C). Set Clock style to Digital in Boox’s screensaver settings for this face.
Your picture, filling the screen or shown whole, with an optional caption along the bottom.
Your note, set as large as it fits.
Who to return the tablet to if it is found. Best on a tablet that leaves the house.
Only the date and a small accent-coloured lamp.
Each plate is drawn on a see-through sheet with a soft paper edge, so it stays readable over whatever is on the screen.
When you last used the tablet, rounded down to the refresh step. It is exact when you start the sleep with Sleep now.
Events from your calendars in the next seven days.
Calendar access is off, so events stay hidden until you allow it.
A short public-domain line, a new one each day.
Leave room for the Boox clock
Keeps the top of the screen free for the clock that Boox draws over the sleep screen. You choose that clock in Boox’s screensaver settings.
That picture could not be read.

Boox dithers every picture itself, turning shades into patterns of dots that e-ink can show. Pre-dithering does it first, with 16 levels per colour, which can look finer on a Kaleido screen. Pre-dithering does not dither text.
Faces use the real weights of the font you choose, including each weight of a variable font. Fonts you keep on the Fonts page appear in this list.
The accent fills shapes such as the lamp, today’s date and the needle. Kaleido shows solid areas of colour best, so text always stays black or white.
While the tablet is awake, redraw every

Boox reads the picture once, when the tablet goes to sleep, so on its own nothing on it changes while the tablet sleeps. The updates under While asleep change that.\nBooxUltimatum also redraws the face when the battery, the date, the calendar, the rotation or your settings change. It skips the redraw when nothing on the face would change.
A wall clock in the style of Braun, with the date, the battery and how long the tablet has slept. With updates while asleep it keeps time. Without them, the hands show when the tablet was put down.
The time set as large as the screen allows, with the date under it and the battery, time asleep and next event along the bottom. Without updates while asleep, it shows when the tablet was put down.

A readout of the sleep itself: how long the tablet has slept, and the battery on a tuning scale with its use and rate. It also counts down to the next event and shows the next alarm. It needs updates while asleep to change.
How long the tablet has slept and how much battery it has used. Shown when updates while asleep are on.
Drawn the same way as the sleep screen, as it would read 1 h 25 min into a sleep with updates while asleep turned on. Tap it to see it at full size.
This face is made for updates while asleep. Turn them on below to keep the face current while the tablet sleeps.

Live updates redraw the face while the tablet sleeps, so the date, battery and agenda stay current. They also cover the bar Boox draws while charging, and Boox’s own clock if you show one. The time you put the tablet down stays as it was.\nEach update wakes the screen for about a second and a half. Measured on a Note Air6 C, the one-minute step cost about 1.6 mAh an hour, and the five-minute step wakes the screen a fifth as often. That is why the one-minute step runs only while charging.
The one-minute step runs only while charging. On battery the shortest step is %1$d minutes, so the screen doesn’t wake 60 times an hour.
No updates on battery, so nothing wakes the screen.
While updates are paused, the sleep screen keeps its last picture and says “Paused until” at its top edge, followed by the hour you set.

Android hides app windows while the tablet is locked, except the overlay from an accessibility service, so BooxUltimatum holds the picture in one. It can’t read the screen or what you type, and it shows nothing while the screen is on.

Boox removes the wake-up alarms of apps it restricts, so updates stop. Allow background usage for BooxUltimatum on Android’s battery page, and if updates still don’t arrive, turn it off and on once. With Shizuku, tap Register with Boox to do that for you.
Lets updates run on the minute. Without it, they can arrive late.
The accessibility service is on, but Android hasn’t started it yet. Leave this page and come back. That usually starts it.
Live updates redraw a full-screen picture, so they work only in Sleep image mode. A plate can’t be updated this way, because Boox reads its sticker only when the tablet goes to sleep.
Apply a face first. Live updates redraw the face you applied.
The tablet hasn’t slept with live updates on yet.

Last sleep: %1$d updates, the last at %2$s.

resources.string: Last sleep: no updates were due.

The last sleep got no updates. Boox’s power manager most likely removed the wake-up alarm. Turn Allow background usage off and on again on the battery page, or, with Shizuku, tap Register with Boox, then try another sleep.
Keeps the sleep screen current while the tablet sleeps

Lets BooxUltimatum redraw its sleep screen at the interval you choose while the tablet sleeps. Android hides ordinary app windows while the tablet is locked but not the overlay from an accessibility service, so this service exists only to hold that picture. It can’t read the screen, can’t see what you type and performs no actions. It shows nothing while the screen is on.
This face is now the sleep screen.

The plate is now written to Boox’s sticker. BooxUltimatum can’t see which sleep screen style Boox uses. Unless Boox is set to Transparent with the sticker on, you still see the picture Boox showed before.
Boox’s default picture is back. To use your earlier style again, choose it in Boox’s screensaver settings.
Sleep now needs Shizuku. Over Transparent can work without it if you allow BooxUltimatum to write Boox’s sticker, as described below.
Mode changed. Tap Apply to pass the new mode to Boox. Until then the last picture stays and BooxUltimatum no longer redraws it.
Published %1$s · drawn in %2$d ms, compressed in %3$d ms · %4$s · %5$s
Checked %1$s · nothing on the face changed, so the file was left as it is
Drawn the same way as the published picture. Dashes mark where Boox draws its clock when you leave room for it. Tap the preview to see it at full size.

For a clean face, open Boox screensaver settings. Set Clock style and Text display to None, and turn Bottom status bar off. That bar adds the battery and “Press power button to wake up”, and Boox shows it while the tablet is charging, whatever the setting. To keep a live time instead, leave Clock style on Digital and turn on Leave room for the Boox clock, or choose Under the clock.
A sticker is a see-through picture that Boox lays over the screen it kept when the tablet went to sleep. Boox needs you to choose it once. After that BooxUltimatum keeps it up to date.

BooxUltimatum can’t see which style Boox is set to. Until you set Boox to Transparent with the sticker on, Boox keeps showing the last sleep picture it was given. After a switch from Sleep image, that older picture is what the tablet shows when it sleeps.

If an older BooxUltimatum picture is still in Pictures, BooxUltimatum can’t remove it. Android doesn’t let an app change a picture it no longer owns, so the newest copy is written beside it. You can delete the old one in Files.
Tap Put in Sticker album below. The current plate appears in the gallery’s Sticker album.

Open Boox screensaver settings, choose Transparent and turn on Show lockscreen sticker. Then tap Select sticker, the + tile, the Sticker album and the BooxUltimatum picture, and confirm the crop with OK.
Come back here and tap Apply. BooxUltimatum finds the sticker Boox saved and redraws it for you.
The plate is in the Sticker album.

Boox draws its clock, the motto and the bottom status bar over any style. You can turn each off in Boox screensaver settings. Restore can’t read the style you had before, so it sets the Boox default picture. Choose your former style in Boox afterwards.
With a PIN, a tablet put to sleep from the lock screen shows a black privacy screen instead (seen on a Note Air6 C). Boox decides this, and BooxUltimatum can’t change it.
Shizuku is running, so the plate is written through it. Nothing else is needed.
BooxUltimatum finds the sticker Boox saved by looking in the Sticker album. Allow it to read pictures for that. It looks at nothing else.
Android asks whether BooxUltimatum may change Boox’s sticker picture. If you allow it, BooxUltimatum keeps the plate current without Shizuku.
BooxUltimatum may write the sticker itself, so no Shizuku is needed for the plate.
BooxUltimatum can’t see a sticker in Boox’s Sticker album. If Android is set to share only some pictures with BooxUltimatum, allow all of them. Otherwise, do the four steps above first.
Android didn’t allow BooxUltimatum to change the sticker picture, so it can’t keep the plate current by itself. Start Shizuku from Access instead.

Boox scales the sticker to fill the screen and keeps only the middle. Plates stay inside the middle area that both orientations keep, so one file works in portrait and landscape. In Boox’s screensaver settings you can also set the scale to fit, which shows the whole sheet.
Write a note in BooxUltimatum › Sleep to show it here.
Choose a picture in BooxUltimatum › Sleep.
This needs Shizuku. Start it from Access, then try again.
No Boox sticker yet. Follow the steps under Boox settings to choose the BooxUltimatum sticker once.
BooxUltimatum could not save the plate in its own files.
BooxUltimatum isn’t allowed to write Boox’s sticker yet. Tap Ask Android to allow it, or start Shizuku from Access, then tap Apply again.
BooxUltimatum could not back up the sticker Boox made, so it left the sticker as it was.
BooxUltimatum couldn’t write the sticker. Check that Boox’s sticker is still in the Sticker album, then tap Apply again.
BooxUltimatum couldn’t restore Boox’s own sticker: %1$s. You can choose another picture in Boox’s screensaver settings.
Sleep screen set to the %1$s face in Sleep image mode
Sleep screen set to the %1$s plate in Over Transparent mode
Sleep screen restored to the Boox default picture
Power-off screen set to the %1$s face
Power-off screen restored to the Boox default picture
The Boox power-off screen is restored.

This sets the picture the tablet shows while it is off, drawn in portrait. It needs Sleep image mode. The battery and the put-down time are left out, and a live face is replaced by the Almanac, because a clock would stop. Boox keeps a copy, so the picture stays as you set it. After you change the face, update it again.

A cube clock drawn in true perspective. The time is on the side facing you, the date on the side in shade, and a round button in the accent colour on top. The shadow is shaded with dots or lines. Without updates while asleep, it shows when the tablet was put down.
The hours and minutes on split-flap cards, with the upper flap leaning back on its hinge and the date on small flaps below. Without updates while asleep, it shows when the tablet was put down.

A grid of tiles. The time and the date, with the week, always show. You choose the others below: the battery and what it has used, time asleep, the alarm, next events, how far through the day and the year you are, the moon, and the home screen’s weather with the time it was read.
The time in words, lit in a grid of letters. The words change every five minutes, and dots in the accent colour count the minutes in between. The letters are in English.
The whole day on one 24-hour ring. Today’s events are arcs, the sleep so far is in the accent colour, and a hand shows now. The night is shaded once the home screen has a weather city.
Today along a line. Events are blocks, the sleep so far is in the accent colour, and a marker shows now. The time and readings sit above.
A Braun-style LCD clock with seven-segment figures, small fields for the date, time asleep, battery and alarm, and a row of buttons with one in the accent colour.

Today’s sun and tonight’s moon. The sun’s path, sunrise and sunset are worked out on the tablet for the home screen’s weather city, the only place BooxUltimatum knows. Without a weather city, the sun follows the clock and the face says so. The moon’s phase needs no place.

A newspaper front page. The headline is the next event or the quote, as you choose below. The weather and battery sit in small boxes beside the title, and columns cover the sleep, what’s ahead and the almanac. The issue number is the day of the year.
The year at a glance, with a dot for every day. Past days are filled, today is in the accent colour, and the face shows how far through the year you are.
Your selected face, %1$s, is in the other tab.
The 24-hour dial turns its hour hand once a day, with midnight at the top.
The time and date always show. Weather shows only if the home screen has loaded it in the last three days. Next events need calendar access and stay hidden without it.

The words change every five minutes, and the dots add the minutes in between. With an update step of 5 minutes or more, updates while asleep land on a whole five minutes, so the dots stay dark while the tablet sleeps.
Sunrise and sunset need a weather city on the home screen. It’s the only place BooxUltimatum knows.
Without calendar access or an event this week, the quote of the day takes the headline.
The sun stays up all day
The sun stays down all day
